Guinea Pigs require a lot of space to run around in their cage. They also require floor time, but that isn't relevant to this topic.

My pigs have a CNC cage, which stands for Cubes And Chloroplast. It is a build-it-yourself project because most cages form the pet store are way too small. The Cubes are actually from a wire shelving unit, the kind that you can use in laundry rooms or kids' rooms. These shelf kits come in wire grids with plastic attachments. Chloroplast is what sign makers use for signs. It is a fairly sturdy plastic, but easy to score into with an exacto knife so you can fold up the edges and is waterproof. Guinea pigs will also sometimes chew on the plastic edges, but they won't eat it.

When I say guinea pigs need a lot of space in their cage, I mean a lot. To put it in perspective, one guinea pig would need a cage that is about 75 by 90 cm, or around .7 square meters. In using the cube grids for building the cage, that would be about 2 by 3 grids. More is always preferred, because guinea pigs love to run around their cage.

Since I have two guinea pigs, I have a bigger cage. My cage is a bit longer than five feet, and about two feet wide. Since I already have the cage built, I can't really show that process, but I do have a couple pictures.

This is the cage without any bedding. You can kind of tell that I messed up a bit scoring the chloroplast in the second half of the cage. Luckily, the cage area is still big enough for my pigs, and I use that area for storage. Soon though, it will actually support the ramp up to the still under-construction second level of the cage. I still have to get more chloroplast and build the actual ramp though.

This is the cage with bedding in it. I use just basic aspen shavings. Other wood shavings, like pine, should be avoided because they can actually cause respiratory (and other) problems for small pets. Even things like pine need to be avoided for other, bigger pets like dogs too. Aspen shavings are good because they don't contain the natural toxins and chemicals of other woods like pine.

Since there is nothing else really in the cage in these pictures, you can kind of get a grasp on the size of the cage I have built. It is actually big enough for three guinea pigs currently (Shh, I do have my birthday coming up and March in my area is also usually 'adopt a guinea pig' month ran by the humane society). The grids are held together by zip ties, and the chloroplast pieces and corner are held together by packing tape, which is also pretty okay for pigs to chew on, but they won't eat it.

If you have any questions about the cage, feel free to ask!

There has been a lot of talk on this site with regards to how to setup a democratic method for removing mods as a result of abuse and content manipulation, but I would like to argue that such an idea is misguided.

There is no feasible way for a community to hold moderators accountable for censorship without involving an administrator.

To that end, it seems that an easier solution would be to preempt any potential ideological censorship by moderators by creating a site wide rule which states that a moderator will be removed from their position if they remove any content that is not spam or in violation of the site wide rules.

In this way, Atko and his fellow admins can hold mods to the standard of free flowing information upon which this site is based.

This is also not to say that mods cannot create sidebar guidelines for the way in which users should be voting within their communities to encourage the posting of relevant content.

If a step like this is not taken by the admin team, this medium will very quickly run into the very same issues of moderator abuse under the guise of "enforcing sidebar rules" as occured on reddit.
Issue an administrative directive preventing moderators from enacting any rules/guidelines which go beyond removing spam and enforcing the site wide rules.

This place is a work in progress, but you can help get it there faster. I would like to create a space where something that approaches formal debates can happen. Of course, this is an online medium and one that doesn't allow for debate-style moderation and speaking turns. However, I think we can come up with a set of rules that allow for something more or less like that to take place.

Please comment here if you have any ideas or would like to contribute.

Initial thoughts

There are just some of ideas I idea I've had for how to implement this sub. Feel free to discuss them as well as anything anyone has brought up in the comments.

  1. The sub itself would heavily moderated to only allow content of the pre-determined type ([Suggestion], [Debate], etc).
  2. [Suggestion] posts for debates people want to see.
  3. Official [Debate] posts that are heavily moderated or otherwise restricted to the approved debaters (or perhaps just the top comments must be by approved debaters). By having prior approved debaters flair can be implemented to distinguish those for or against, among other things.

Maybe implement a posting format.

Something like this in the title of the post "[Opinion or Statement/ Poster is Arguing for or Against/Will Respond or Won't Respond to Comments/ Allow Links to Support Evidence or Won't Allow Links]" could quickly allow the potential debater to decide if they want to partake in the debate.

It should also be reminded to the poster and the commeters that these debates should not be taken personally, to help prevent degeneration of civil debates. And if it is possible, Debates shouldn't be voted on, or else outside viewers may upvoat or downvoat a debate without participating (and potentially allowing unknowing commentors to put in their opinions).

All good suggestions.

I think some of the site features might be need to be fully implemented before something like this can work. For example, while there is an option to restrict submissions to approved users, there doesn't seem to be any way to specify who those users are.
